transcript.text: Hi everyone. So, Eli, you've asked to borrow my PA system for a wedding reception this Sunday. Before I make any decision, I'd like you to restate the exchange offer and the schedule you're proposing -- what you're offering in return and when you'd collect and return the equipment. Then, June, I'd like you to confirm the venue's operating limits so I know what we're working with.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks, Rosa. Here's the exchange offer and schedule: In return for borrowing your PA system, I'm offering 36 boxed lunches for the reception — 30 regular and 6 vegetarian — with no cash payment involved. For the schedule, I'd pick up the PA on Saturday at 10 AM and return it on Sunday at 8 PM, after the reception wraps up. June, whenever you're ready, could you confirm the venue's operating limits so Rosa has the full picture?
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I can confirm the venue's operating limits. Only 600 watts remain available on the venue's shared circuit because the kitchen warmers use the rest. Rosa's two standard speakers together draw 450 watts, which is within the limit. However, adding the powered subwoofer would raise the total load to 750 watts, which would overload the circuit. So the PA can be used with the two speakers only — the subwoofer cannot be used at this venue.
